(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Rockstar Games still won't reveal just how much GTA 6 has cost to develop, but one person involved has shot down the idea that the game has a $1.5 billion budget. Given the 13-year wait for GTA 6, it's probably safe to assume that Rockstar and Take-Two have spent a lot of money on the project. The game has been worked on in one way or another since at least the mid 2010s, with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson confirming the studio was working on a version of the game dubbed "Project Americas" - which would've seen the story take place across both North and South America - back in 2015 before the studio shifted focus to work on Red Dead Redemption 2 . Rockstar and Take-Two have kept quiet on just how much the game has and will cost to develop, but a popular guess came from analyst Michael Pachter, who estimated that development costs would exceed $1.5 billion last year, which has since become a popular assumption online. Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: Speaking to Bloomberg 's Jason Schrier, Rockstar Games ' head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, was asked about the game's budget. While no concrete answer was given, Schrier notes that she shot down the rumor that the game would surpass $1.5 billion. Granted, that doesn't mean the game's budget won't be one of the largest in gaming history - I'd be surprised if it wasn't - but until the actual number is shared, we won't know for sure. That being said, GTA 6 is likely going to be a massive release, with everyone expecting it to be one of the biggest game launches of all time - if not the biggest - after 13 years of feverish hype. Given that co-studio head Aaron Garbut said the game doesn't compromise on detail or scale , I'd wager that Rockstar is confident it'll recoup whatever it spent on GTA 6 pretty quickly.
